extracted.intended_audience: designers, marketers, communicators, and students creating infographics (including instructors and business professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating compelling infographics that tell a visual story and for planning their release online and in print (includes design rules, storytelling structure, SEO/release strategy, and special formats like resumes and internal/confidential uses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tells a story visually / engaging story built with data
rubrics_metrics.description: A cool infographic tells a story visually — an engaging story built with your data. More than just using pictures or colorful charts, infographics create the type of visual information that your audience will quickly grasp and remember.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on narrative using data; aim for visual information that attracts attention, is easier to understand, and is more likely to be remembered. Avoid treating infographics as mere decoration or random charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure information into a simple 3-part story
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure information into a simple 3-part story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize content so the infographic presents a clear beginning, middle, and end (a concise story arc) to make the message easy to follow and memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the design process and follow infographic design rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the design process and follow infographic design rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a defined process for planning, designing, and producing infographics; follow best-practice design rules and be aware of common mistakes to avoid (the book covers best practices and pitfalls).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass the 5-second rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Will your infographic pass the 5-second rule?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the main point can be grasped in about five seconds — the visual hierarchy, headline, and lead graphics should communicate the core message immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend data visualizations with text, illustrations and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Blend data visualizations with text, illustrations and images to tell a complete story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine charts, narrative text, icons/illustrations and imagery so they complement each other and produce a coherent story rather than competing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent data sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly cite data origins and be transparent about methodology and provenance to build credibility and allow verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose engaging topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging topics are essential for effective infographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select topics that will interest your target audience and are likely to attract attention and sharing; topic choice affects whether an infographic will succeed online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan infographics to match goals (brand, traffic, product explanation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different goals require different types of infographics (e.g., build brand equity, drive website traffic, explain product features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define the objective up front and design content, tone, length, and distribution to serve that objective rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement a complete infographic release/SEO strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement a complete infographic release strategy to maximize SEO results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider keywords, embed code, online lifespan, meta data, landing pages and tactics to get posts and links from other sites; a full release plan affects discoverability and viral potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design infographic resumes by combining resume best practices with viral design
rubrics_metrics.description: Design a personal infographic resume to market yourself. Good infographic resumes combine the best practices from traditional resume design and viral online infographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain clarity, relevant structure and readability from traditional resumes while applying visual design and viral-friendly presentation where appropriate for recruiters/audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt infographics for internal/confidential use (presentations/print)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal Confidential Infographics: adapt online infographic approaches for internal use where confidential data is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use infographic techniques for presentations and printed handouts internally, selecting elements that work in those media and respecting confidentiality (avoid public release of sensitive data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design clear data visualizations (use appropriate chart types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design great infographics with clear data visualizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure charts and graphics are clear and appropriate for the data and message; follow visualization best practices to avoid misleading or confusing representations and consult the 'toolbox' of visual techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate software, tools and data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about the software applications and websites used by designers. Designing infographics is a combination of visualizing data, creating custom illustrations, editing images and putting together the complete design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose tools suited to the task (data viz, illustration, image editing), and use recommended data sources; the right toolset speeds production and improves quality.
